name: LL-37

track.title: Lab & animal
track.line: Cell and animal studies of infection and wounds

track.title: Phase II

track.title: FDA approval
track.line: Not approved; FDA lists safety concerns

what.text: LL-37 is a chain of 37 amino acids. It is the only cathelicidin, a family of germ-killing (antimicrobial) peptides, that the human body makes. It is cut from a larger precursor protein called hCAP18. Skin, the gut, the airways, the testis and several kinds of white blood cells make it.

src.label: Dürr UH, et al. Biochim Biophys Acta 2006 (review)

what.text: In lab work, LL-37 kills a wide range of bacteria and also acts on the immune system: it can dampen or steer inflammation, draw immune cells to a wound, bind bacterial toxins, and help skin cells cover a wound.

src.label: Dürr UH, et al. Biochim Biophys Acta 2006 (review)

what.text: The body makes LL-37 on its own. Injected or applied LL-37 is a drug that no regulator has approved.

research.text: LL-37 has been tested in people in a few small trials, mostly as a cream or solution put on chronic wounds. The largest trial, with 148 people with leg ulcers, did not meet its main goal. No trial has tested it for muscle or injury recovery.
Each study is listed below as it was run.

research.meta: Sweden · 2014 · Randomized, placebo-controlled trial (first in humans)
research.title: Hard-to-heal venous leg ulcers, 2014 (Sweden)

facts.v: 3-week placebo run-in, then randomized, double-blind treatment with one of three strengths of LL-37 (0.5, 1.6 or 3.2 mg/mL) or placebo, put on the ulcer twice a week
34 adults with venous leg ulcers that had not healed
4 weeks of treatment and 4 weeks of follow-up
safety and the rate of wound healing

research.found: The two lower strengths had healing rates about six and three times higher than placebo (only the lowest was statistically significant). The highest strength did no better than placebo. There were no local or whole-body safety concerns. The first author worked for Pergamum AB, a drug company.

src.label: Grönberg A, et al. Wound Repair Regen 2014

research.meta: Poland and Sweden · 2021 · Phase IIb randomized, placebo-controlled trial
research.title: HEAL LL-37: venous leg ulcers, 2021

facts.v: double-blind, randomized, three groups: LL-37 at 0.5 or 1.6 mg/mL, or placebo, put on the ulcer twice a week along with compression bandaging (EudraCT 2018-000536-10)
148 adults with hard-to-heal venous leg ulcers, mean age 67.6, at 15 sites
3-week run-in, 13 weeks of treatment, 16 weeks of follow-up
main goal: confirmed complete closure of the ulcer by week 13

research.found: In the whole group, LL-37 did not improve healing compared with placebo. A post hoc look at people with large ulcers (at least 10 cm²) found better healing measures with LL-37; this was not the planned main analysis. 12 serious adverse events occurred in 11 people (7.4%); none was judged related to the drug. Three authors worked for Promore Pharma, which developed the drug.

src.label: Mahlapuu M, et al. Wound Repair Regen 2021
Mahlapuu M, et al. Wound Repair Regen 2021, full text (PMC9298190)

research.title: Diabetic foot ulcers, 2023 (Indonesia)

facts.v: randomized, double-blind: LL-37 cream or placebo cream twice a week, on top of standard wound care (NCT04098562)
25 adults aged 18 to 60 with diabetic foot ulcers that were uninfected or mildly infected (13 on LL-37, 12 on placebo)
4 weeks
wound healing (granulation index), two inflammation markers and bacteria counts

research.found: The granulation index rose more in the LL-37 group at each weekly check. Inflammation markers and bacteria counts did not differ between groups. One person on LL-37 had mild skin irritation from wound fluid. The authors declared no conflicts of interest.

src.label: Miranda E, et al. Arch Dermatol Res 2023
Miranda E, et al. Arch Dermatol Res 2023, full text (PMC10514151)
ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04098562

research.title: LL-37 injected into melanoma, MD Anderson (NCT02225366)

facts.v: open-label dose-finding study; no control group
4 enrolled adults with melanoma; results posted for 3
LL-37 injected into tumors once a week, at two dose levels
up to 8 weeks
side effects, to find a dose, and immune response

research.found: The posted results list no serious adverse events and no deaths. Other events included anemia, low white blood cell counts, raised bilirubin and skin changes. No paper reporting the results was found.

src.label: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02225366

research.title: Oral LL-37 made by bacteria, in COVID-19, 2023 (China)

facts.v: open-label, randomized, placebo-controlled, single center. The product was Lactococcus lactis bacteria engineered to make LL-37 in the gut, not the peptide itself.
238 adults in hospital with the Omicron variant
time until virus tests turned negative, and adverse events

research.found: Virus tests turned negative sooner with the product than with placebo when it was started early. No severe adverse events were seen. This tested a live bacterial product, so it does not tell us about injected LL-37.

src.label: Zhao Y, et al. J Med Virol 2023

research.text: No trial has tested LL-37 by injection for muscle, tendon or sports injuries. ClinicalTrials.gov lists no such study.

us.text: LL-37 is not FDA approved for any use. FDA lists it on its Category 2 page (bulk drug substances that may present significant safety risks in compounding), among nominations that were later withdrawn. It is not one of the six peptides in the October 2026 HHS compounding policy. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: none. Drugs@FDA lists no approved drug containing cathelicidin (LL-37).

src.label: Drugs@FDA via openFDA, search for cathelicidin

items.text: FDA lists “cathelicidin LL-37” among bulk drug substances “nominated but withdrawn” from its safety-risk category. FDA says compounded LL-37 “may pose risk for immunogenicity for certain routes of administration and may have complexities with regard to peptide-related impurities and API characterization.” It adds: “FDA lacks sufficient safety-related information regarding cathelicidin LL-37 to know whether the drug would cause harm when administered to humans. Nonclinical research findings suggest detrimental effects on male reproduction and that this drug can be protumorigenic in some tissues.”

src.label: FDA, bulk drug substances that may present significant safety risks (Category 2 page)

items.text: the HHS enforcement discretion policy published October 30, 2026 covers only BPC-157, TB-500, epitalon, semax, KPV and MOTS-c. LL-37 is not among them.

after.title: Sport
after.text: LL-37 is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List. Class S0 (non-approved substances) bans at all times any pharmacological substance not covered by another class that has no current approval by any government health authority for human use, such as drugs still in clinical development. No regulator record found approves LL-37. Whether WADA applies S0 to LL-37 was not confirmed. The 2027 list adds “peptides” to the examples in S0; WADA says peptides not approved for human use may be prohibited even if not named.

side.text: In the small wound trials, LL-37 put on the skin raised no safety concerns. FDA, however, says it lacks the safety data to know whether LL-37 would cause harm, and points to animal and lab findings on male reproduction and tumor growth.

items.text: possible immune reactions, impurities, and “nonclinical research findings” that “suggest detrimental effects on male reproduction and that this drug can be protumorigenic in some tissues.” These findings come from animal or lab studies, not from people.

items.text: no local or whole-body safety concerns in the 34-person trial. In the 148-person trial, 12 serious adverse events (the most common was the skin infection erysipelas) occurred in 11 people; none was judged related to LL-37.

surprises: LL-37 is the body’s own wound-defense peptide, yet the largest trial (148 people with leg ulcers) did not improve healing overall, and FDA lists concerns about male reproduction and tumor growth.
